question: Using Section 9E.12 and Figure 9E-12, state the minimum bicycle-box length, required pavement symbol, turn-on-red rule, and green-pavement coverage rule.
model_answer: Direct Answer: A bicycle box, if used, must be at least 10 feet long (measured from its upstream edge nearest the motor-vehicle stop line to its downstream edge nearest the crosswalk or intersection) and must contain at least one bicycle symbol marking. Turns on red are prohibited from any lane where a bicycle box is placed. Green-colored pavement is optional in a bicycle box, but if used it must cover the full limits of the box, and green pavement generally is limited to specific bicycle applications, including bicycle boxes. Standards (mandatory): - "If used, the distance from the upstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest to the stop line for motor vehicles to the downstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest the crosswalk or intersection shall be at least 10 feet. At least one bicycle symbol marking (see Figure 9E-12) shall be used in the bicycle box." - "Turns on red shall be prohibited from the lane where a bicycle box is placed." (Section 9E.12 Standard, shown on the full page view of the section text.) - "If used, green-colored pavement shall be used in the full limits of the bicycle box." (Section 9E.12 Standard, shown on the page containing Figure 9E-12, Sheet 1 of 2.) - "If used, green-colored pavement shall be limited to: A. Bicycle lanes …, B. Extensions of bicycle lanes through intersections …, C. Extensions of bicycle lanes through areas where motor vehicles enter a mandatory turn lane …, D. Two-stage bicycle turn boxes …, E. Bicycle Boxes (see Section 9E.12), and F. As a background for bicycle detector symbols …" Options (permitted): - A bicycle box may be used to increase the visibility of stopped bicycles on the approach to a signalized intersection during the red portion of the signal cycle for the approach lane(s) behind the box. - "Green-colored pavement may be used in a bicycle box." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 9E-12 (Sheet 1 of 2) shows a bicycle box across one lane with a "10 ft MIN." dimension between the intersection stop line and the advance stop line, a bicycle symbol inside the box, and green-colored pavement labeled "(optional)." [Image 6] The full page view of Section 9E.12 shows the Standard text including the 10-foot minimum, the bicycle symbol requirement, and "Turns on red shall be prohibited from the lane where a bicycle box is placed." [Image 7] The full page with Figure 9E-12 (Sheet 1) shows the Standard "If used, green-colored pavement shall be used in the full limits of the bicycle box." [Image 5] Figure 9E-12 (Sheet 2 of 2) shows a bicycle box across multiple lanes with the "10 ft MIN." dimension and the required NO TURN ON RED (R10-11) sign, consistent with the turn-on-red prohibition. [Image 4] Figure 9E-11's page also displays the Section 9E.12 Standard provisions, including the turn-on-red prohibition. Citations: - Section 9E.12 Standard §6 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Option §1 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Option §12 (p.1106) - Section 3H.06 Standard §2 (p.626) - Figure 9E-12 (p.1106) - Figure 9E-11 (p.1105) - Page 1146 - Page 1147 - Page 1148
gold_answer: The bicycle box must be at least 10 feet long, include at least one bicycle symbol, prohibit turns on red from its lane, and, if green pavement is used, fill the entire limits of the box.
